check: whether any of the 129 GameTests needs an external mod on the classpath, which the smoke classpath does not provide
why: The integration matrix is NOT_RUN precisely because the smoke harness loads only three jars - fabric-api, the mod and the harness - so a GameTest depending on Tectonic, C2ME, FTB, RoadWeaver, Xaero, Voxy or OpenCL would fail for want of the mod rather than for a code reason. The 23 never-run cases make that worth checking before rather than after.
result: None does. Searching the whole gametest source set for those seven names returns no match in any file.
scanValidated: The same search finds GameTest 493 times, Fixture 379 and assert 500, so the absence is real rather than a broken pattern.

theCaseThatLookedLikeItMight.whyItLookedRisky: Its name refers to gate negotiation, a RoadWeaver interop concept, and the integration matrix lists a RoadWeaver patched row
theCaseThatLookedLikeItMight.whatItActuallyImports: local.plaincraft.greatwall.compat.road.RoadTypes, WallArchBackfill, DeterministicHash and its own WallTypes - all in-mod types
theCaseThatLookedLikeItMight.itsOwnDescription: Driven against the real GateLedger and the pure RoadTypes DTOs
theCaseThatLookedLikeItMight.verdict: It exercises this mod's own compatibility types, so no external jar is needed.

alsoConfirmed: No class named Stress, Fault or Smoke sits in the gametest source set, so the harness classes stay out of the suite.
whatThisAdds: Discovery is now checked four ways for the pending run: every class is a registered entrypoint, none carries a batch attribute so all fall in defaultBatch, none needs a structure template beyond the API-provided empty one, and none needs an external mod. The 23 first-time cases have no known obstacle to running.
